messages:
morgan: FYI PR #5078 (kv-cache eviction tweak) on canary shows ~12% p95 increase for longseq workloads. Uploaded gist + flamegraphs: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-5078. Can @leo @ciara take a look? This is blocking the ramp for the new canary group. :warning:

leo: on it, grabbing canary traces and logs now. will post a quick summary.

ciara: re-running the standard longseq workload locally (seq_len ~4096). I'm seeing similar bump. Quick numbers below:

```
Workload       p95    p99    throughput
baseline       220ms  340ms  125req/s
pr-5078        246ms  380ms  121req/s  (+12% p95, -3% tput)
mem RSS        baseline: 1.1GiB  pr: 1.28GiB (+180MiB)
```

morgan: commit abc1234f - change is 'disable_eviction_during_microbatch' and adjust eviction window. My hypothesis: increased in-memory KV due to skipped evictions -> more GC/CPU contention leading to tail latency.

jess: I left inline comments on the PR about the eviction invariants and a missing unit test for the eviction scheduler. small change but high impact.

leo: looked at heap profiles from canary — kv_map size grows steadily under longseq; GC cycles are more frequent. The eviction scheduler never triggers under the new microbatch path because the batch loop bypasses the check. easy to reproduce in the perf harness.

ciara: quick experiment: toggled evict_every from 500 -> 200 and re-ran. Results:
```
pr-5078+evict200 p95: 225ms
RSS: down ~120MiB
throughput ~ baseline
```
So lowering interval recovers most of the regression.

morgan: thanks — two options: revert the change (safe) or add an adaptive eviction threshold (better long-term). I prefer revert + iterate, since this affects end-user latency. @jess can you push an expedited revert if CI looks good?

jess: will open a revert PR now (5079). ping me when CI finishes on the revert and I'll approve asap. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for pr-5078 at 2026-03-17T14:08:32Z

morgan: note: this only impacts longseq paths (>2048 tokens). Short sequences unchanged. Also added benchmark artifacts to the PR.

leo: I can add a microbenchmark to the runtime test harness to catch the bypassed eviction check. I'll create a ticket and prototype a test.

ciara: running revert locally then pushing a canary patch to validate recovery. will post numbers in ~10m.

jess: revert PR 5079 is up, CI started. I'll approve once tests green.

deploy-bot: revert PR 5079 merged and canary redeployed at 2026-03-17T14:31:10Z

morgan: initial canary metrics after revert look good — p95 back to ~222ms and RSS back to ~1.12GiB. Closing loop for now. We'll follow up with a small RFC for an adaptive eviction approach and add the microbenchmark to CI. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :tada:
